record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: For the Stable Roommates problem, compute p_n, the probability that a uniformly random instance of size n admits a stable matching, and in particular determine the asymptotic behavior of p_n as n becomes large.

evidence.quote: A long-standing open problem, formulated as Problem 8 in Gusfield and Irving [45], is the computation of p_n, the probability that a random instance, chosen uniformly from all possible sr instances of size n, admits a stable matching. Of particular interest is the asymptotic behaviour of p_n, as n grows large.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Stable Roommates problem on an even number n of agents. An instance consists of n agents, each of whom provides a strict total ordering (preference list) of the remaining n-1 agents. A matching is a partition of the n agents into n/2 unordered pairs. A pair {a,b} of agents who are not matched to each other blocks a matching M if a prefers b to its partner in M and b prefers a to its partner in M. A matching is stable if no blocking pair exists.

Equip the set of all instances of size n with the uniform probability measure (equivalently, each agent's preference list is chosen independently and uniformly at random from the (n-1)! possible orderings). Let p_n denote the probability that a uniformly random instance admits at least one stable matching.

Determine p_n exactly, and determine the asymptotic behavior of p_n as n → ∞.
artifact.status_search_result: Historically posed as Problem 8 of Gusfield–Irving. Pittel and Irving (1994) gave an upper bound (≈ e^{1/2}/2 ≈ 0.8244) and a lower bound for p_n. Mertens' numerical simulations conjectured p_n = Θ(n^{-1/4}). A 2026 preprint by Chin and Michelen ("The random stable roommates problem typically has no solution") proves p_n → 0 as n → ∞, confirming the Gusfield–Irving conjecture that stable matchings are atypical. The precise asymptotic rate (e.g., the conjectured Θ(n^{-1/4})) does not appear to be fully established, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The random stable roommates problem typically has no solution
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the first vanishing upper bound on the probability that a stable matching exists, confirming Gusfield–Irving's conjecture that p_n → 0.
status_evidence.claim: p_n tends to 0 as n grows, resolving the qualitative version of the open problem.

status_evidence.title: The 'Stable Roommates' Problem with Random Preferences (Pittel & Irving)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes non-trivial upper bound e^{1/2}/2 ≈ 0.8244 on the limsup of p_n and a lower bound of order (4e^3/(πn))^{1/2}.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier bounds on p_n were known but the precise asymptotic remained open.

status_evidence.title: Stable Roommates Problem with Random Preferences (Mertens)
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical simulations suggest p_n behaves asymptotically like Θ(n^{-1/4}).
status_evidence.claim: Conjectured asymptotic rate not yet rigorously established.
